title: Battle of Schliengen: The Spy Who Turned the French Victory into Deception
hook: A secret French spy's fake order changed the outcome of the 1796 Battle of Schliengen.
description:
A secret French spy's fake order changed the outcome of the 1796 Battle of Schliengen. Discover how deception reshaped a pivotal clash in the French Revolutionary Wars.

Subscribe for more hidden twists in history's greatest battles.
#History #BattleOfSchliengen #MilitaryDeception #historyfacts #shorts

beats.say: The night before Schliengen, a French spy slipped a falsified order into Austrian camps, sowing chaos.
Austrian commander Prince Charles demanded a retreat, but his lieutenant, General Wartensleben, ignored it, trusting the false intel.
At dawn, Austrian artillery opened fire on empty fields, believing the French were withdrawing toward the Rhine.
Meanwhile, French General d'Andelot seized the moment, positioning his infantry behind the hills of Kandern.
The Austrian cavalry, confused, charged uphill into a hidden French ambush, suffering heavy losses.
A lone Austrian cannon, nicknamed 'the thunderer', burst, killing d'Andelot's second-in-command, General de Vaux.
The French, enraged, pressed forward, turning the battlefield into a chaotic melee of musket fire.
By noon, the Austrians retreated across the Rhine, leaving behind abandoned supplies and shattered morale.
The false order remained undiscovered until weeks later, when a captured French courier confessed the ruse.
History credits Schliengen to French brilliance, but the real victor was deception, not swords.
